chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not eat the meats of the jallalat — and these are the animals that eat human excrement — and if any of their sweat touches you, then wash it off.

key_terms.الْجَلَّالَاتِ: Jallalat — animals (typically livestock such as chickens, sheep, cows) that habitually eat human excrement; their meat and milk become forbidden due to the impurity of their diet
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةَ: 'Adhira — human excrement/feces; specifically human waste as opposed to animal dung
key_terms.عَرَقِهَا: Sweat of the jallalat animal; physical contact with their sweat requires washing due to ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Is it haram to eat meat from animals that eat human excrement (jallalat) according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits the consumption of meat from jallalat — animals that feed on human excrement — and additionally rules that contact with their sweat necessitates washing. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential concern with ritual purity (tahara) in dietary laws. The term 'jallalat' refers specifically to animals whose primary food source is human waste, a dietary contamination considered to render the animal's meat impure and its consumption forbidden.
